summary: Invoice rounding discrepancy between Console estimate and finalized bill for cached-response traffic
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a $5–6 discrepancy between the cost estimate displayed in the Redwood Console for a 24h window and the finalized invoice line for the same window. The customer indicates the traffic was dominated by cache hits (we returned cached completions for repeated prompts).

Impact: SummitRetail is an enterprise customer running high-volume product search augmentation. The variance affects their month-end reconciliation and they have paused autopay pending clarification. Potential customer churn risk if unresolved.

Environment: Production (us-west region), traffic primarily to redwood-open-13b via hosted API with caching enabled at the gateway layer.

Observed numbers: Console estimate (2026-03-08 UTC): $3,421.58. Final invoice line (2026-03-08): $3,426.12. Delta: $4.54 (0.13%). Customer provided a CSV of sample requests showing cache_hit=true for ~72% of requests.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use SummitRetail org key to send 10k repeated prompts that should trigger prefix cache hits.
2) Observe Console estimated spend under Billing -> Cost Explorer for the 24h window.
3) Wait for hourly reconciler to produce the finalized invoice lines (or run billing dry-run for the same window).
4) Compare per-request token rounding and per-invoice line rounding.

Expected: Console estimate and final invoice line should match within rounding error tolerance (<= $1 for this workload).
Actual: Finalized invoice is larger by $4–6 for the window in question.
logs:
customer-provided-sample-requests.csv attached in ticket (10 rows sample). Relevant billing reconciler logs: billing/reconciler/us-west/2026-03-08.log lines 1241-1253 show per-request token_charge rounding to 2 decimal places before aggregation. Gateway logs: gateway-usw-01 cache_hit=true header present for 72% of requests.

Snippets:
[reconciler] 2026-03-08T03:12:11Z request_id=abc123 token_units=0.333333 billed_units=0.33
[reconciler] 2026-03-08T03:12:12Z request_id=def456 token_units=0.666667 billed_units=0.67
[gateway] 2026-03-08T03:12:11Z request_id=abc123 cache_hit=true cache_key=sku-lookup-7
comments: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage added billing and metering teams, requested raw CSV of requests and sample reconciler logs from customer. Customer says they need explanation before autopay resumes.

2026-03-10 11:03 - Diego Morales (BillingENG): Noted the reconciler currently applies per-request rounding to 2 decimal places on token units before summing. This behavior differs from Console estimator which aggregates raw token fractions and rounds at the final aggregation stage. Filed INT-2041 to propose change.

2026-03-11 08:42 - Lina Chen (SRE): Confirmed gateway sends cache_hit header; cache-hit responses include smaller token fractions which amplify rounding noise when rounded per-request. Attached query to billing DB showing 12,345 cache-hit requests with mean token_units 0.34.

2026-03-11 14:12 - SummitRetail (Customer): Thanks for the update. We need to understand whether the difference will be corrected on our current invoice or if a credit will be issued. Autopay is on hold until resolved.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Diego Morales (BillingENG): Proposed workaround: run invoice-recalc in 'aggregate-first' mode for affected window and produce manual credit if recalculation matches Console. Raised a quick patch PR to billing aggregator to make aggregation mode configurable.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: The reconciler's per-request rounding to two decimal places causes rounding-up bias on many small cached responses. Console estimator aggregates raw token fractions across the window and only rounds at currency formatting, producing a slightly lower estimate. Evidence: DB aggregate vs sum(per-request-rounded) shows +$4.54 delta for the window.

Tech details: billing service uses 'per_request_rounding=2' by default for performance reasons. Cache-hit responses produce token fractions <1 which are sensitive to per-request rounding. Tax conversion (USD->EUR) not a factor here (customer in USD).

Next steps: 1) Run aggregator in aggregate-first mode for exact window. 2) Produce provisional credit if recalculated invoice is lower. 3) Implement short-term config toggle to use aggregate-first for orgs flagged as enterprise. 4) Longer-term: change default reconciler behavior to aggregate raw token fractions and round once at final stage to reduce bias.
resolution: Workaround applied: BillingENG ran a manual recalculation for SummitRetail's 2026-03-08 window using aggregate-first mode. Recalculated invoice delta: -$4.54 matching Console estimate. A provisional credit of $4.54 was queued and will appear on the next billing cycle. Patch PR created to make aggregate-first mode toggleable; rollout scheduled to prod during low traffic window.
resolution_notes:
2026-03-12 16:20 - Diego Morales: Manual recalculation completed and provisional credit approved. Credit reference CR-2026-0312-571829. PR #472 merged to feature-flag aggregate-first mode: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/472. Follow-up task INT-2041 tracks default behavior change and test coverage.

Customer-facing note sent: explanation of rounding and confirmation of credit. Finance notified to apply credit and to confirm autopay resumption is safe.
customer_communication: 2026-03-12 17:00 - Aisha Patel to SummitRetail: We investigated and found the difference was caused by per-request rounding on many small cached responses. We have recalculated the window using aggregate-first rounding and queued a $4.54 credit to your account (ref CR-2026-0312-571829). Autopay can be re-enabled at your discretion. We are rolling out a fix to avoid this class of discrepancy in future invoices and will follow up once the feature-flag rollout is complete.
